title: A subscription tracker that shows every renewal before it happens.
seoTitle: Subscription Tracker App for Android, Free | RenewRadar
description: A free subscription tracker app for Android. Every subscription and trial on one screen, monthly and yearly totals, and reminders before each renewal.
lede: Streaming, music, cloud storage, software, gym, news. RenewRadar puts all of it on one screen, sorted by what is charged next, with a reminder before each payment.
content:
Why track subscriptions at all

Subscriptions are designed to be forgotten. Each one is small, the charge arrives on a different day of the month, and the receipt goes to an inbox nobody reads. Over a year, a handful of $5 to $15 plans quietly adds up to hundreds.

A subscription tracker fixes the two things that make this happen: you cannot see everything in one place, and nothing warns you before a charge. RenewRadar does both, without asking for access to your bank or cards.

Adding a subscription takes about a minute

Start typing a name and RenewRadar suggests popular services, with a category and a usual billing cycle filled in. Then enter:

  • Price and currency. Any currency with a three-letter code, such as USD, EUR, GBP or PHP.
  • Billing cycle. Weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearly, or a custom number of days.
  • Next charge date. After it passes, RenewRadar moves it forward by one cycle on its own.
  • Category and who it is for. Personal, work or business, so you can tell them apart later.
  • Reminders. 14, 7, 3 or 1 day before, or on the day. Pick as many as you like.

If the subscription starts with a free trial, turn on the trial switch and add the trial end date and the price after the trial. Trials then get their own countdown. See free trial reminders.

One screen, sorted by what is charged next

Home is split into a few short sections so you can read it at a glance:

  • Trials come first, sorted by end date, with the days left.
  • Due this week holds anything charged in the next seven days.
  • Later this month holds the rest of the current month.
  • Subscriptions lists everything else in renewal order.

Each row shows the service, the price and how many days are left, with a color that turns warmer as the date gets close.

Monthly and yearly totals that add up

Comparing a weekly plan with a yearly one is hard in your head. RenewRadar converts every billing cycle to a monthly figure (a yearly price divided by 12, a weekly price times 52 divided by 12) and shows a monthly and yearly total at the top of Home.

The Stats screen breaks that down by category, so you can see that streaming is half of your spend before you decide what to cut. Free trials are not counted until they turn into a paid plan, and paused or cancelled items are left out.

Want a quick number before installing anything? Try the subscription cost calculator.

Pause, cancel and restore

Real subscriptions are messy. You pause a gym for the summer, cancel a streaming service and sign up again for one show, or switch a plan from monthly to yearly. RenewRadar handles each case:

  • Pause keeps the item but stops reminders and leaves it out of totals.
  • Mark as cancelled moves it to a Cancelled list at the bottom of Home.
  • Restore brings a cancelled item back and moves a past renewal date forward.
  • Edit any detail. Reminders are rescheduled every time you save.

Free and Pro

The free version tracks up to five active subscriptions and trials, with reminders, countdowns and totals. Cancelled items do not count toward the five.

Pro is a single one-time purchase (US$9.99 in the United States, shown in your currency on Google Play). It removes the limit and adds detailed reports for the next 12 months, your biggest costs, and a CSV export of your full list. It never renews.

title: Try it free, and cancel before the first charge.
seoTitle: Free Trial Reminder and Tracker App | RenewRadar
description: A free trial tracker and reminder app for Android. RenewRadar counts down every trial, shows the price after it ends, and notifies you before the first charge.
lede: A free trial is only free if you remember when it ends. RenewRadar counts down every trial and reminds you with enough time to decide.
content:
Why free trials turn into charges

Free trials work because they need a payment method up front and renew on their own. The end date is usually 7, 14 or 30 days away, far enough to forget, and the confirmation email is easy to lose. By the time you notice, the first month or the whole year has already been charged.

Most services let you cancel during the trial and keep using it until the trial ends. The hard part is not cancelling. It is remembering to do it in time.

How trial reminders work in RenewRadar

When you add a subscription, turn on Free trial and enter two things: the day the trial ends and the price you will pay afterwards. From then on:

  • The trial sits in its own Trials section at the top of Home, sorted by end date.
  • Each trial shows a countdown, such as 2 days left, and the price after the trial.
  • Reminders count down to the trial end, not to a later renewal.
  • The trial is not added to your monthly total until it becomes a paid plan.

Reminders are notifications scheduled on your phone, so they arrive even if you have not opened RenewRadar in weeks, and they work offline.

Choosing the right reminder time

You can pick any mix of 14, 7, 3 and 1 day before, or the same day. The default is 3 days and 1 day before. A few rules of thumb:

Trial typeSuggested remindersWhy
7-day trial3 days and 1 day beforeEnough time to try it properly and still decide.
30-day trial7 days and 1 day beforeA week out is a good moment to ask whether you used it.
Trial that becomes a yearly plan14, 7 and 1 day beforeA yearly charge is large and harder to get refunded.
Service with a cancellation notice periodAdd the notice to your timingSome plans must be cancelled a few days before the end date.

When the trial ends

If you cancelled, mark the trial as cancelled in RenewRadar so it stops reminding you. It moves to the Cancelled list, where you can restore it later if you sign up again.

If you decided to keep it, edit the item, switch off Free trial, and it becomes a regular subscription with renewal reminders and a place in your totals.

A trial you have not touched stays at the top of Trials marked as ended, so it is hard to miss.

Tips for safer free trials

  • Add the trial the moment you sign up. You know the end date then; a week later you will not.
  • Check where you are billed. Trials started in an app are often billed by Google Play or the App Store, not by the service. Our cancellation guide shows where to cancel each one.
  • Cancel early if you can. Many services, including subscriptions billed through Google Play, let you keep access until the paid period would have started.
  • Note the price after the trial. Introductory prices often jump after the first period.

title: A subscription reminder app that tells you before you pay.
seoTitle: Subscription Reminder App for Android | RenewRadar
description: A subscription reminder app for Android. Get notified days before every renewal and free trial charge, at the timing you choose. No bank login.
lede: Most charges you regret are charges nobody warned you about. RenewRadar sends a reminder before every subscription renews, at the timing you choose, so every payment is a decision.
content:
Why you need subscription reminders

Subscriptions renew on their own. Your bank tells you after the money has gone, and most services send at most one email, easy to miss among everything else. A subscription reminder app works the other way round: it warns you before the charge, while you can still cancel, switch plans or simply confirm you want to keep paying.

How reminders work in RenewRadar

Add a subscription with its price, billing cycle and next renewal date. RenewRadar then schedules notifications on your phone:

  • Timing per subscription: 14, 7, 3 or 1 day before, or on the day. Pick one or several.
  • A clear message: for example Netflix renews in 3 days. $15.99 will be charged on Nov 2.
  • Defaults in Settings, so new subscriptions get your usual timing automatically.
  • Automatic roll-forward: after each renewal, the next date and the next reminders are set for you.

Reminders that arrive without the app or internet

Reminders are local notifications scheduled by Android, not messages from a server. They arrive at 9 in the morning on the day you chose, even if you have not opened RenewRadar for weeks and even without a connection. On phones with strict battery saving, allowing RenewRadar to run without battery restrictions keeps them on time; our Android reminder guide shows how.

Free trial reminders too

Free trials get their own reminders that count down to the end of the trial, with the price that starts afterwards: You will be charged $11.99 on Oct 30 unless you cancel. Read more about free trial reminders.

Which timing to choose

  • Yearly plans: 14 days and 3 days before, time to compare and decide.
  • Monthly plans: 3 days and 1 day before.
  • Weekly plans: 1 day before.
  • Free trials: 3 days and 1 day before the trial ends.

Private by design

RenewRadar never asks for your bank login, card number, email or name. Your subscriptions are stored only on your phone. It is free for up to five subscriptions and trials, and Pro is a one-time purchase, never another subscription.

Renewals are easy to forget

A monthly charge reminds you that a subscription exists twelve times a year. A yearly renewal appears once, usually as a surprise, often at a higher price than the first year. Domains, antivirus, VPNs, storage plans, memberships and annual software licences all work this way.

A renewal tracker that keeps the dates for you

A renewal notification before every charge

Choose when to be notified for each subscription: 14, 7, 3 or 1 day before, or on the day. A yearly plan can warn you two weeks ahead and again three days before, while a monthly one reminds you the day before. Each notification shows the amount and the date, for example Amazon Prime renews in 7 days. $139.00 will be charged on Oct 25.

Decide at every renewal

See which months will be expensive

Monthly and yearly totals sit at the top of Home. With Pro, a report lists the charges expected in each of the next 12 months, so big yearly renewals never arrive unannounced. Read how to plan your next 12 months of charges.

Free to start

title: Subscriptions in more than one currency, tracked honestly.
seoTitle: Multi-Currency Subscription Tracker for Android | RenewRadar
description: Track subscriptions billed in different currencies. RenewRadar records each one in its own currency and shows honest totals per currency, without guessed exchange rates.
lede: A streaming plan in pesos, cloud storage in dollars and a newspaper in euros. RenewRadar keeps each one in the currency you are actually billed in.
content:
Who needs a multi-currency tracker

More people pay in several currencies than you might think:

  • People who moved abroad and still pay for services at home.
  • Freelancers and remote workers who pay for tools in US dollars while earning in another currency.
  • Anyone whose app store charges in the local currency while websites bill in dollars or euros.
  • Families who share plans across countries.

Most trackers assume a single currency, or convert everything with a rate that may not match what your bank actually charged.

How currencies work in RenewRadar

Every subscription has its own price and its own currency. When you add one, USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD, PHP, INR and JPY are one tap away, and you can type any other three-letter currency code, such as SGD, MXN or BRL.

You also choose a default currency in Settings, which is filled in for new subscriptions so you do not have to pick it every time.

Prices are stored exactly as you enter them. Reminders show the amount in the original currency, so the number in the notification matches the number on your statement.

Why totals stay per currency

Exchange rates move every day, and banks and card networks add their own margins. A converted total can look precise and still be wrong by several percent.

So when your subscriptions use more than one currency, RenewRadar shows a separate monthly and yearly total for each currency instead of guessing a rate. Spend by category on the Stats screen works the same way. You always see real amounts you will actually be charged.

If all your subscriptions use one currency, you simply get one monthly and one yearly total.

Tips for tracking mixed currencies

  • Use the currency on the receipt, not the one your bank converts it into. That is the amount that will be charged again.
  • Check card fees. Some cards add a foreign transaction fee to every charge in another currency, which can make a local plan cheaper.
  • Watch app store pricing. Google Play and the App Store charge in your local currency, often at different prices from the service's website.
  • Review yearly plans. A large yearly charge in another currency is exposed to a whole year of exchange rate changes.

Bank-linked apps can find subscriptions automatically by reading your transactions. In exchange, a third party gets ongoing access to your financial history, and the app usually only works with banks in certain countries.

A manual tracker asks for about a minute per subscription. In exchange, nobody else sees your spending, it works in any country and with any card or wallet, and it keeps working without internet.

What stays on your phone

Everything you enter is stored in the app's private storage on your phone: names, prices, currencies, billing cycles, dates, categories, notes and reminder settings. Reminders are local notifications created on the phone itself, not sent from a server.

There is no RenewRadar account, so there is no profile, email address or password to leak.

The only network requests the app makes

RenewRadar makes two kinds of requests, and neither contains your subscriptions:

  • A weekly service list. A plain file of popular service names, categories and colors that powers the suggestions when you type a name.
  • Purchase checks. If you buy Pro, Google Play processes the payment, and RevenueCat confirms the purchase using a random anonymous ID.

The details are in the privacy policy.

What RenewRadar does not do

  • No bank or card connections.
  • No accounts, emails or phone numbers.
  • No ads, advertising IDs or analytics.
  • No selling or sharing of data, because there is none to share.

Keeping a copy of your list

Because nothing is stored on a server, uninstalling the app removes your list. Pro users can export the full list as a CSV file at any time and save it wherever they like, through the share sheet. The file goes only where you send it.

title: What do your subscriptions really cost?
seoTitle: Subscription Cost Calculator: Monthly, Yearly and 5-Year Cost | RenewRadar
description: Free subscription cost calculator. Add your streaming, music, software and other plans to see what they cost per month, per year and over five years.
lede: Add what you pay for, in any billing cycle. The calculator shows the true monthly, yearly and five-year cost. Nothing you type leaves your browser.
content:
How to use the result

The yearly figure is the one to look at. Most people underestimate it, because each subscription is charged separately and never shows up as one number. Once you see it, ask three questions about each line:

  1. Did I use it in the last month? If not, it is a candidate to cancel or pause.
  2. Am I paying for the same thing twice? Two music services, two cloud storage plans, or a family plan and a personal one.
  3. Is there a cheaper way to pay? Yearly billing, a family plan, or a bundle often costs less than monthly plans on their own.

Our 20-minute subscription audit walks through this step by step.

Frequently asked questions

How is the monthly cost calculated?
Every price is converted to a monthly figure. Monthly prices stay the same, yearly prices are divided by 12, quarterly prices by 3, and weekly prices are multiplied by 52 and divided by 12, because a month is slightly longer than four weeks.
Is my data saved or sent anywhere?
No. The calculator runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you type is stored or sent to a server, and it is gone when you close the page.
Why is the five-year figure so high?
Because subscriptions repeat. A $12 monthly plan looks small, but it is $720 over five years. The five-year number is simply the monthly total times 60, before any price increases.
Can I mix currencies?
The calculator uses one currency for all rows. If you pay in several currencies, run it once per currency, or use RenewRadar, which keeps a separate total for each currency.

title: How to Cancel a Free Trial Before You Are Charged
seoTitle: How to Cancel a Free Trial Before You Are Charged | RenewRadar
description: Where to cancel a free trial on Google Play, the App Store and websites, how early to do it, and how to make sure you are never charged by surprise.
lede: Cancelling a free trial is usually quick. The tricky part is knowing who bills you and doing it in time. Here is how to get both right.
content:
1. Find out who bills you

The same service can bill you in different ways depending on where you signed up. This decides where you cancel:

  • Started in an Android app and paid through Google Play: cancel in Google Play.
  • Started on an iPhone or iPad and paid through Apple: cancel in your Apple account settings.
  • Started on the service's website with a card or wallet: cancel in your account on that website.
  • Added through a phone carrier, bank or bundle: cancel with that provider.

Not sure? Search your email for the sign-up confirmation. The sender (Google Play, Apple or the service itself) tells you who bills you.

Uninstalling an app does not cancel its subscription or trial. You have to cancel it where you are billed.

2. Cancel a trial billed through Google Play

  1. Open the Google Play Store app.
  2. Tap your profile picture in the top right.
  3. Tap Payments & subscriptions, then Subscriptions.
  4. Choose the trial and tap Cancel subscription.
  5. Follow the steps to confirm.

Google Play sends a confirmation email. In most cases you keep access until the end of the trial. Our Google Play guide covers the web version and what happens next.

3. Cancel a trial billed through the App Store

  1. Open Settings on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Tap your name at the top, then Subscriptions.
  3. Choose the trial and tap Cancel Free Trial or Cancel Subscription.

If you do not see the trial there, it is probably billed by the service directly or through Google Play.

4. Cancel a trial on a website

For services you signed up for on the web, cancellation is in your account on that website. Look for Account, Billing, Plan or Membership. A few things to watch for:

  • Several steps. Some sites show offers before the final cancel button. Keep going until you see a confirmation.
  • Notice periods. Some plans must be cancelled a set number of days before the trial ends. Check the terms when you sign up.
  • Pause is not cancel. Pausing usually restarts billing automatically later.

5. When to cancel

If you already know you will not keep it, cancel the same day you sign up. Many services, including subscriptions billed through Google Play, keep the trial running until its end date after you cancel.

If you want to decide later, set reminders for a few days before the end, not on the last day. Time zones and billing systems do not always charge at midnight in your time zone, so the last day can be too late.

RenewRadar does exactly this: add the trial with its end date and the price afterwards, and it reminds you before the trial ends. See free trial reminders.

6. Confirm the cancellation worked

  • Keep the confirmation email until the date has passed.
  • Check the subscription list where you cancelled. It should show an end date instead of a renewal date.
  • Look at your statement after the trial end date. If you were charged anyway, contact the service or the store with your confirmation. Google Play and Apple both have refund request pages.

title: How to Cancel a Subscription on Google Play
seoTitle: How to Cancel a Subscription on Google Play (Phone and Web) | RenewRadar
description: Cancel any subscription billed through Google Play from your Android phone or the web, and learn what happens to access, refunds and data after you cancel.
lede: Subscriptions and trials you started in an Android app are usually billed by Google Play. Here is how to cancel them in under a minute.
content:
Cancel on an Android phone or tablet

  1. Open the Google Play Store app.
  2. Make sure you are signed in to the Google account you subscribed with.
  3. Tap your profile picture in the top right corner.
  4. Tap Payments & subscriptions, then Subscriptions.
  5. Select the subscription you want to cancel.
  6. Tap Cancel subscription and follow the instructions to confirm.

Uninstalling the app does not cancel the subscription. You will keep being charged until you cancel it in Google Play.

Cancel on the web

  1. Go to play.google.com and sign in with the same Google account.
  2. Open your account menu and choose Payments & subscriptions.
  3. Open Subscriptions, choose the one to cancel and select Cancel subscription.

The web version is useful when the subscription is on a phone you no longer have.

What happens after you cancel

  • You keep access for the time you have already paid for, including the rest of a free trial.
  • You get an email from Google Play confirming the cancellation. Keep it until the end date has passed.
  • No automatic refund. Cancelling stops future charges. For a charge you did not want, use Google Play's refund request, or contact the app's developer.
  • The app's data stays with the service. Cancelling does not delete your account with that service. Delete it separately if you want to.

Cannot find the subscription?

If it is not listed in Google Play, it is billed somewhere else:

  • Another Google account. Switch accounts in the Play Store and check again.
  • The service's website. If you signed up on the web, cancel in your account there.
  • Apple. If you subscribed on an iPhone, cancel in your Apple account settings.
  • A carrier or bundle. Some plans are billed through a phone or internet provider.

Our guide to cancelling a free trial explains how to find out who bills you.

Pause instead of cancel

Some apps let you pause a Google Play subscription for a while instead of cancelling. If the option is available, you will see it in the same Subscriptions screen. Billing restarts automatically when the pause ends, so set a reminder for that date. In RenewRadar, mark the item as paused and edit the next charge date when it resumes.

title: The 20-Minute Subscription Audit
seoTitle: The 20-Minute Subscription Audit: Find and Cut Recurring Charges | RenewRadar
description: A simple routine to find every subscription you pay for, decide what stays, cancel the rest and keep it that way, in about 20 minutes.
lede: Set a timer, grab your phone and your last two bank or card statements. By the end you will know exactly what you pay for, and you will probably pay for less.
content:
Step 1: Find everything (8 minutes)

Subscriptions hide in several places. Check each of these:

  • Bank and card statements for the last two months. Look for the same merchant appearing every month, and for small amounts you do not recognize.
  • Google Play: Play Store, profile picture, Payments & subscriptions, Subscriptions.
  • Apple: Settings, your name, Subscriptions, if you have an iPhone or iPad.
  • Your email: search for receipt, renewal, subscription and trial.
  • PayPal or other wallets: look for automatic payments or approved merchants.
  • Phone and internet bills: bundles and add-ons are often charged here.

Two months of statements matter because quarterly and yearly plans will not show up in a single month.

Step 2: Write it down in one place (5 minutes)

For each subscription, note the name, the price, how often it is charged and the next charge date. Converting everything to a monthly figure makes them comparable: a yearly price divided by 12, a weekly price times 52 divided by 12.

You can do this on paper, in a spreadsheet, in our subscription cost calculator, or directly in RenewRadar, which also reminds you before each charge.

Step 3: Keep, downgrade or cancel (5 minutes)

Go down the list and give each item one label:

LabelWhen to use it
KeepYou used it in the last two weeks and would sign up again today at this price.
DowngradeYou use it, but a cheaper tier, a family plan, an ad-supported plan or yearly billing would do.
RotateStreaming services you watch in bursts. Keep one at a time and switch every month or two.
CancelYou have not used it in a month, or you pay for something similar elsewhere.

Watch for duplicates: two cloud storage plans, music included in a bundle you already pay for, or both a personal and a family plan.

Step 4: Act on it right away (2 minutes)

Cancel the items marked Cancel now, while you are motivated. Most services let you keep access until the end of the period you already paid for, so there is nothing to gain by waiting.

See how to cancel on Google Play and how to find who bills you.

Keep it that way

An audit works once. Staying on top of subscriptions needs two habits:

  1. Log every new subscription and free trial the day you sign up, with its end date or next charge date.
  2. Get a reminder before every charge, so each renewal becomes a small decision instead of a surprise.

That is what RenewRadar is for. It is free for up to five subscriptions, has no account and never connects to your bank.

title: Like Bobby, but for Android.
seoTitle: Bobby Alternative for Android: Manual Subscription Tracker | RenewRadar
description: Bobby is a popular manual subscription tracker for iPhone. RenewRadar brings the same simple, private approach to Android, with free trial countdowns and multi-currency support.
lede: Bobby made manual subscription tracking popular on the iPhone. If you are on Android, RenewRadar follows the same idea: add what you pay for by hand, see the totals, and get reminded in time.
content:
Why people look for Bobby on Android

Bobby is a well-liked iOS app for keeping a manual list of subscriptions. It is available only for iPhone and iPad, so Android users, and people who switch from iPhone to Android, need something else.

What RenewRadar has in common with Bobby

  • Manual entry. No bank connection; you add each subscription yourself.
  • Reminders before renewals on the device.
  • Totals so you can see what everything costs together.
  • Free to start, with a one-time upgrade rather than another subscription.

Side by side

BobbyRenewRadar
PlatformiPhone and iPadAndroid
Bank connectionNoNo
Account neededNoNo
Free trial countdown sectionNo dedicated sectionYes, trials first with days left
Per-subscription reminder timingYesYes: 14, 7, 3, 1 day or same day
Multiple currenciesYes, totals converted to a base currencyYes, totals kept per currency without guessed rates
Sync between devicesiCloud sync with the upgradeNo, your list stays on your phone
PricingFree for 5; small one-time upgradeFree for 5; Pro one-time US$9.99

Bobby details are based on its App Store listing and public reviews as of November 2026 and may change. Bobby is a trademark of its owner; RenewRadar is not affiliated with it.

What RenewRadar adds

  • Free trials come first. A dedicated Trials section shows the days left and the price after the trial, and reminders count down to the trial end.
  • Due this week and later this month. Home groups what is coming up next.
  • Personal, work or business. Tag each subscription by who it is for.
  • Pause, cancel and restore without losing the details.
  • Pro reports and CSV export for the next 12 months of charges.

If you are moving from an iPhone, add your subscriptions from Bobby's list into RenewRadar with their next charge dates. It takes about a minute each.

title: Privacy Policy
seoTitle: Privacy Policy | RenewRadar by Pixel DevCode
description: How RenewRadar handles your information. Your subscription data stays on your device.
content:
In short: the subscriptions and free trials you add stay on your phone. We do not run any server that receives them, and RenewRadar has no accounts, no ads, no analytics and no bank connection.

1Who we are

RenewRadar ("the app") is published by Pixel DevCode ("we", "us"). You can contact us at renewradar@pixeldevcode.com.

2Information that stays on your device

Everything you enter is stored only on your phone, in the app's private storage:

  • Your subscriptions and free trials: names, prices, currencies, billing cycles, renewal dates, categories, reminder settings, notes and colors.
  • Your settings, such as your default currency, default reminder timing and light or dark theme.

We cannot see this information and do not receive a copy. If you uninstall the app, it is deleted from your phone. If you want to keep a copy first, use the export feature described below.

3Reminders

Reminders are local notifications created by the app on your phone. They do not use a push notification service, and no information is sent to us to produce them. The app asks for your permission to show notifications, and you can turn them off at any time in your phone's settings.

4Network connections the app makes

The app makes only two kinds of network requests, and neither contains your subscription data.

  • Service list update. About once a week the app downloads a plain list of popular service names, categories and colors from renewradar.pixeldevcode.com to power the name suggestions when you add a subscription. The request contains no information about you or your subscriptions. As with any web request, the server that hosts the file (GitHub Pages) can see your IP address and standard request details.
  • Purchases. The optional one-time Pro unlock is processed by Google Play. We use RevenueCat, a purchase-management service, to confirm whether the unlock is active on your device and to restore it if you reinstall. RevenueCat receives a randomly generated anonymous app user ID, your purchase status and technical details such as the app version, device type and IP address. We do not receive your payment details, and the app does not send it your subscriptions. See RevenueCat's privacy policy and Google's privacy policy.

5Exporting your data

With Pro, you can export your subscriptions as a spreadsheet (CSV) file. The file is created on your phone and handed to your phone's share sheet. It goes only where you choose to send it, and we never receive it.

6What we do not do

  • We do not create accounts or ask for your name, email address or phone number.
  • We do not connect to your bank or read your payments.
  • We do not show ads, use advertising identifiers or sell any data.
  • We do not use analytics or tracking tools inside the app.

7Children

RenewRadar is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect information from them.

8Your choices and rights

Because your subscription data never leaves your phone, you control it directly: you can edit or delete any item in the app, export it, or remove everything by uninstalling the app. For questions about purchase data held by RevenueCat or Google, or to exercise any data rights you may have where you live, contact us at renewradar@pixeldevcode.com.

9This website

This website is a set of static pages. It sets no cookies and uses no analytics or third-party scripts or fonts. If you pick a color mode, that choice is remembered in your browser's local storage on your device. The subscription cost calculator runs entirely in your browser, and nothing you type into it is stored or sent anywhere. Like any web host, GitHub Pages may log visitors' IP addresses for security and operations.

10Changes to this policy

If we change how the app handles information, we will update this page and the date above. Material changes will also be noted in the app's release notes.

11Contact

Pixel DevCode
renewradar@pixeldevcode.com

content:
In short: RenewRadar helps you keep track of subscriptions and free trials, but you stay responsible for cancelling them in time. Pro is a one-time purchase through Google Play, tied to your Google account, and refunds follow Google Play's refund policy.

1Agreement

These terms apply to the RenewRadar app ("the app"), published by Pixel DevCode ("we", "us"). By installing or using the app, you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the app. Your use of Google Play is also covered by Google's own terms.

2What the app does

RenewRadar lets you list your subscriptions and free trials by hand, see what they cost, and get reminders before renewal and trial end dates. The app does not connect to your bank, does not cancel subscriptions for you, and does not know about charges you have not entered.

Totals and renewal dates are estimates based on what you enter. They are for your own planning and are not financial advice.

3Free version and Pro

  • The free version lets you track up to five active subscriptions and trials. Cancelled items do not count toward this limit.
  • Pro is an optional one-time purchase that unlocks unlimited items, detailed spending reports and CSV export. It is not a subscription and does not renew.
  • Pro is linked to the Google account you used to buy it. You can restore it on a new phone or after reinstalling by signing in to Google Play with the same account and tapping Restore purchase in Settings.
  • "Lifetime" means for as long as we offer the app on Google Play. Features we add later may or may not be part of Pro.

4Payments and refunds

All payments are handled by Google Play. We never see or store your payment details. Prices are shown in the app and on Google Play before you buy, and may vary by country.

Refunds are handled under Google Play's refund policy. You can request one from Google Play directly. If you have a problem with your purchase, you can also email us and we will try to help.

5Promo codes

We may give out Google Play promo codes for Pro. Each code works once, has no cash value, cannot be exchanged for money, and may have an expiry date. Codes are redeemed through Google Play and are subject to Google's terms.

6Reminders

Reminders are local notifications scheduled on your phone. We make a reasonable effort to deliver them on time, but delivery depends on your phone. Notification permissions, battery-saving settings, Do Not Disturb, the phone being off, or changes made by the phone maker can delay or block them.

You are responsible for checking the actual renewal and trial end dates with each service and for cancelling in time. We are not responsible for charges you receive, including charges after a reminder was late, missed, or based on a date that was entered incorrectly.

7Your data

Your subscriptions are stored only on your phone, as described in our Privacy Policy. Because we do not keep a copy, we cannot recover your data if your phone is lost or reset or the app is uninstalled. Pro users can export a CSV copy at any time.

8Acceptable use

You may use the app for your own personal, work or business tracking. You may not copy, resell or redistribute the app, remove or bypass its purchase checks, or reverse engineer it except where the law allows this.

9Ownership and trademarks

The app, its design and its content belong to Pixel DevCode. Names of subscription services shown in the app belong to their owners and are used only to identify those services. RenewRadar is not affiliated with or endorsed by any of them.

10Changes to the app

We may update, change or stop offering the app or any feature, for example to fix problems, follow store rules or improve it. If we stop offering the app, the version on your phone will keep working with the data already on it for as long as your phone supports it, but it may no longer receive updates.

11No warranty

The app is provided "as is" and "as available". As far as the law allows, we make no promises that it will be error-free, always available or suitable for a particular purpose.

As far as the law allows, Pixel DevCode is not liable for indirect or consequential losses, or for subscription charges, fees or lost savings related to your use of the app. Our total liability for any claim about the app is limited to the amount you paid for Pro, or US$10 if you did not buy Pro.
